finding: Empirical validation of Spike #122 hypothesis: build truth-shape fingerprint from project notebooks via srmech v0.4.1rc14 primitives; measure spectral discrimination against 4 adversarial contrast classes (citation_swap / value_mutation / vocab_swap / random_baseline).

Implementation: char-level co-occurrence graph Laplacian (n=64 alphabet) + character-frequency state-vector projection via srmech.spectral.decompose; pairwise similarity via srmech.spectral.similarity (HDC bytes) + cosine on real-coefficient vectors (robust check).

ALL 5 contrast classes return identical real-coefficient similarity to truth fingerprint: real_sim_mean = 0.9856, std = 0.0082 across attested_held_out / citation_swap / value_mutation / vocab_swap / random_baseline. Cohen's d ≈ 0.000 vs all adversarials (NULL discrimination).

Root cause: random_baseline is character-shuffled, which preserves character-frequency unigram distribution. Since the state vector IS just the unigram frequency, character shuffle preserves the state → preserves projection → identical fingerprint. The chosen fingerprint design captures unigram statistics only; cascade-shape (order-sensitive, positional, n-gram structure) is invisible to it.

The framework's cascade-shape detection hypothesis (Spike #122) is NOT falsified by this result. What's falsified is one specific simple implementation. Cascade-shape lives in HIGHER-ORDER statistics (n-gram order; positional encoding; subword token sequences) that this unigram-Laplacian discards. Per [[user_stance_framework_domain_algebra_not_length_or_magnitude]]: framework predicts structure exists; implementation must be sensitive enough to detect it.
anchor_class: L+I (need order-sensitive cyclic-cascade structure not unigram)
